title: Coordinate decompositions for an additive finite-product equivalence
statement: Let $C$ and $D_i$ be preadditive categories [def-nagata-category, def-weil-preadditive-category], indexed by a finite type $I$, and suppose each $D_i$ has a zero object. Give the product its pointwise preadditive structure. Let $E:C\simeq\prod_i D_i$ be an equivalence whose inverse is additive. There are functors $e_i:D_i\to C$ and coordinate insertions $s_i:D_i\to\prod_kD_k$ with $e_i=s_iE^{-1}$. Their own coordinate restriction is naturally the identity, and each other coordinate object is zero. Moreover, there is a bilimit bicone with point $\operatorname{Id}_C$ for the functors $E\operatorname{pr}_i e_i$, and a bilimit bicone with point $E^{-1}$ for the functors $\operatorname{pr}_i e_i$ on the product. The statement includes the empty index type. No choice of biproduct data in $C$ is required; the two bicones are constructed from coordinate insertions and the equivalence.

proof.text: Define insertion at coordinate i using the given object at i and the chosen zero object elsewhere. Define projection and inclusion natural transformations for each coordinate. Their pairwise composites are the identity on the diagonal and zero otherwise; their diagonal sum is the identity.

Whisker the coordinate bicone through the additive inverse equivalence. On the product side its point is the inverse functor; on the source side conjugate by the unit isomorphism to make the point exactly the identity. Additivity preserves the total sum identity, so isBilimitOfTotal proves both bilimits. The counit supplies the diagonal and off-diagonal comparison formulas.

lean.statement:
theorem equivalenceCoordinateDecomposition
    {C : Type*} [Category C] [Preadditive C] {J : Type*} [Finite J]
    (D : J → Type*) [∀ i, Category (D i)] [∀ i, Preadditive (D i)]
    [∀ i, HasZeroObject (D i)] (E : C ≌ ∀ i, D i) [E.inverse.Additive] :
    ∃ e : ∀ i, D i ⥤ C,
      (∀ i, Nonempty (e i ⋙ (E.functor ⋙ Pi.eval D i) ≅ 𝟭 _)) ∧
      (∀ i k, i ≠ k → ∀ M, IsZero ((e k ⋙ (E.functor ⋙ Pi.eval D i)).obj M)) ∧
      (∃ s : ∀ i, D i ⥤ ∀ k, D k,
        ∀ i, e i = s i ⋙ E.inverse ∧
          Nonempty (s i ⋙ Pi.eval D i ≅ 𝟭 _) ∧
          (∀ k, k ≠ i → ∀ M, IsZero ((s i).obj M k))) ∧
      (∃ b : Bicone (fun i ↦ (E.functor ⋙ Pi.eval D i) ⋙ e i),
        b.pt = 𝟭 _ ∧ Nonempty b.IsBilimit) ∧
      (∃ b : Bicone (fun i ↦ Pi.eval D i ⋙ e i),
        b.pt = E.inverse ∧ Nonempty b.IsBilimit)
